prompt_rules: Descriptions short (3-10 words), no technical instructions; negative prompts are deprecated.
Images to the API by URL, never inline base64 above ~32px (MCP clients truncate it).
Never rescale pixel art: crop an oversized source; unzoom upscaled art before using it as a reference.
Off-palette output is expected: reduce_colors on the whole set in ONE call, then our remap.

create_character_v3.description: 8-direction turnaround of a figure-like (humanoid) sprite from one south reference.

start_image.pose: full-body, neutral standing idle, arms at sides, low top-down, centred
notes: Whatever the sprite faces is taken as south: a 3/4 turn silently offsets the WHOLE set by 45 degrees.
Choose the smallest canvas that still fits; the reference's framing is inherited by all 8 views.
Reject action poses, portrait framing and isometric references.

prompt_rules: PixelLab's own recipe: 'full-body front-facing south-facing idle game character sprite, low top-down view, centered, neutral standing pose with arms at sides'.
Rotate the BODY alone; add wheel/rack/held tools as layers or inpaints after the set exists.
Enable Force symmetry (S/N vertically symmetric, E/W mirrors); flip a good direction for its mirror.

arg_limits.body_class: humanoid (mannequin template only); non-humanoids get limbs added

notes: v3 reference mode supports the mannequin template only; angled or non-humanoid shapes risk poor results.
style_character_id (a completed 8-direction character) or color_image locks the palette.

animate_skeleton.description: Skeleton-driven animation (moves pixels instead of redrawing): the recommended path for character work.

start_image.pose: walks: a MID-STRIDE state; idles: the gated still
notes: A walk described from a standing frame has to invent the stride; one from a mid-stride frame continues it.
Skeleton keypoints must match the image or transparency and colour degrade.

prompt_rules: Animate south first, one direction per call.
Describe motion only, never appearance or environment.
Fixed head 'always' for a stable face.
Even frame counts: 4 idle, 8 walk, 16 complex.
Fix frames by freezing good ones and inpainting the rest (raise init strength).
notes: 2-4 generations per direction.

animate_template.description: Template animation (1 generation per direction) of a managed 8-direction character.

start_image.pose: walks from a mid-stride create_character_state; idles from the still
notes: Walk loops from idle stances are high-risk for closure failures.

prompt_rules: Animate south first, one direction per call.
Motion only; fixed head; even frames (4 idle, 8 walk, 16 complex).

animate_text.description: Text-driven v3 animation of a still (frame 0 stays identical to the input).

notes: Managed characters return 9 images for 8 frames (frame 0 = the input).

prompt_rules: Motion only; one direction per call; even frames; v3 bills on the grown canvas (96px often animates at ~132px).

inpaint.description: Add or change one part on a locked body with a mask.

start_image.pose: the gated BARE body (inpaint onto the body, not onto a body with the part already drawn)
notes: Pro Flash sizes 32-256 in multiples of 4; no images or masks are rescaled.

prompt_rules: Mask: pure black/white, same size as the source; WHITE = generate (v3 / Pro Flash; the Aseprite extension is reversed).
Inpainting never draws outside the mask: mask ALL the space the part may occupy; leave context around it.
Short description of the part (3-10 words).
notes: Held items are layers in PixelLab's own model (paperdoll transfer_outfit, inpaint 'adding equipment').

create_8_direction_object.description: 8 directions of a prop or rigid object from one reference (props only).

notes: Size cannot be set: the image dimensions determine the output size; pad the reference square first.

prompt_rules: Works well for props; identity transfer is unreliable for characters.
Not a 3D rotation: a rigid box may drift; inspect all 8.

reduce_colors.description: Quantize a whole set to a palette image in one call.
prompt_rules: ALL frames in one call ('quantizing them one at a time is the mistake this tool exists to prevent').
notes: Follow with our own Oklab remap for exact adherence.

prompt_rules: Noise words to never write: 'transparent background', 'crisp pixel art', 'pixel-perfect', pixel dimensions, counts, 'spritesheet/grid'.
Never retry an interrupted stream (billed).

generate.description: New still from a prompt (12 variations per 15 credits).
prompt_rules: Describe the subject; sizes and counts go in fields, not prose.
notes: Recommended chain: generate -> clean in editor -> edit into the motion pose -> animate.

edit.description: One change to an existing sprite; keeps the input's size.

notes: First input = primary, up to 9 supporting images.

prompt_rules: Describe only the intended change. State what must stay unchanged.
One change per request; chain results.
Never ask for a sheet of poses.

arg_limits.size: not accepted (API rejects size; output keeps the input size)

style-reference.description: New sprites in the style of 4-8 reference sprites (9 results).
prompt_rules: 4-8 sprites (larger sets may confuse).
Describe the subject, not the style; neutral prompt ('giant' overpowers).
Restate traits that must hold ('no outlines').

direction-set.description: 8 directions of one finished sprite; NO prompt.

start_image.pose: a clean 1:1 sprite with an unmistakable front cue and a different back cue (headlights vs tail lights)
notes: Measured: an unmarked side start gave fronts for backs; front/back cues gave all 8 right; a bulky 96px mech went humanoid at NE/NW.
The docs give no facing rule, so the image must carry it (their example faces east-ish).

prompt_rules: Takes no text prompt: visual cues in the image only.
Output order is NOT positional: read each image's `direction` metadata.
notes: An 88px input came back 64; a 96px mech ~40px and cut.

animate.description: Animate a still into a loop (PNG sheet + WebP + JSON).

start_image.pose: genuine pixel art with a clean grid and a pose suited to the motion (edit into a mid-motion pose before a roll/walk)
notes: Animation must be cohesive with the starting image; clean the still first.
If the animation is wrong: go back to the still, adjust the pose or silhouette, then generate again (never reword).

prompt_rules: Prompt = motion, energy, loop ('seamless loop').
output_frames and colors go in fields, never the prompt; never request a spritesheet.
Never write 'transparent background' or 'pixel art'; prompt a flat contrasting background and set remove_bg.
Training max is 256: never upscale an input.
503s are normal: retry once after minutes; failures refund.

rotate.description: 8 views of an existing sprite ($0.10); always 8, 3x3 sheet optional.

start_image.pose: neutral, tools clearly separated from the body
notes: A 4x display copy is rejected: send the native-resolution frame.
Thin asymmetric props are the likeliest to be redrawn.

prompt_rules: Optional short subject hint only; identity comes from input_image.
return_spritesheet = 3x3 PNG, centre empty, every view facing the centre; frame order starts down-right and turns counter-clockwise, cardinals at 2/4/6/8.
notes: The prompt-driven rd_animation__8_dir_rotation ($0.25, 80x80) invents the design: never for an existing sprite.

walking.description: Walk loop from a cardinal view ($0.14).

notes: Best results when uploading a neutral pose.
A sprite whose opaque pixels touch the canvas edge animates badly.

prompt_rules: Describe MOTION, not the character; weight/speed adverbs help most.
Describe MOTION, not the character.
Describe MOTION, not the character.

rd_pro.description: Still generation with up to 9 reference images ($0.18).
prompt_rules: Reference images guide style and content without being redrawn: generate the character once, then pass that output back as a reference.
input_palette is quantization, not a promise: add return_pre_palette.
Prompt a flat contrasting background + remove_bg: true.
notes: A user__ style can be built from one reference via POST /v2/styles (force_palette, force_bg_removal).

pixel_tools.description: Free pixel-perfecting tools for HD/AI images.
prompt_rules: Pipeline: k_centroid_downscale (width+height required) or Pixel Fixer -> pixel_correction -> palette_converter.

arg_limits.pixel_fixer_dither: fails on heavy dithering; /neural for damaged images

notes: Colours come from the unquantized original.

prompt_rules: One-line prompts: silhouette + unique details; mention the view angle.
Name the distinctive parts in every edit prompt ('chrome arm'); be material-specific.
Keep one resolution tier (16-32 / 48-64 / 96 / 128) for the whole set; size is a hint, not a promise.

generate_game_art.description: Still generation (pixel or HD); the strongest still/edit tool we have.
prompt_rules: Mention the view angle; start around 128px output for character sprites.
Once you have one sprite you like, add it as a style reference for everything else.

arg_limits.colors_note: the API hex palette takes at most 8 colours; 4/8/16/unlimited are guidance

notes: Output is snapped by SpriteCook's grid detector but drifts in size: snap/remap ourselves afterwards.

generate_character.description: Base character (64x64, transparent, perspective baked in, tight crop).
prompt_rules: Match your perspective early: changing perspective after the fact is much harder; the animation won't rotate the view for you.
Generate the base character once, then animate that exact asset_id.
notes: No rotation tool: directions come from the perspective's animation presets.

generate_character_animations.description: Preset motion set on a base character asset id.

start_image.pose: the exact first frame the motion starts from (prep pose; a back-facing run wants the character turned around)
notes: Prep poses are grid-checked against the character's real resolution; a retry 'tends to make the same call' -- fix with the Pro model, more detail, or a regenerated character.

prompt_rules: Keep 'Enhance prompt' ON and prompts short.
Engine v1.1 for anything that must LOOP (walks, idles; even frames); v1.5 for a one-angle action (steadier, stiffer, no negative prompt).
Margins LOW: 0-5% idle, 5-10% attack, 10-15% jump.
notes: Turning a character by edit is NOT documented anywhere.

animate_game_art.description: One motion from an existing asset.

start_image.pose: tight crop of the still the motion starts from
notes: Source <=256px, recommended 64x64; use edge_margin instead of padding the source.

prompt_rules: Short prose prompt from what's visible; enhancer ON.
Frame count is the first knob when motion feels stiff.
notes: In Godot use the OUTPUT frame size (margins enlarge frames); verify frames x width = sheet width.

edit.description: Revise a still (same asset id lineage).
prompt_rules: Repeat the identifying parts each time; one change per edit; keep the resolution tier.
Alpha is faked: exact #00FF00 background + 2-3px white outline, keyed in HSV with despill; never 'transparent'.
Nobody reports any image model honouring a true pixel grid or exact size: all output needs snapping.

generate.description: Concept/anchor render from a general image model (NB2 / NB Pro / FLUX / Qwen).

start_image.pose: reference anchor on a graph-paper grid when deriving views
notes: The south anchor on a grid overlay is 'the most important image you'll generate'.

prompt_rules: ONE view per call: never a whole 8-direction/16-frame sheet in one text call.
Reference + full layout spec + a PRESERVE LIST repeated every call (face, proportions, outline weight, shading; camera, scale, cell size, foot baseline).
Per-view edits: 'change only the facing, keep everything else', chaining anchor + previous view.
'Orthographic projection / flat 2D' stops feet shrinking; attach a graph-paper grid image.
notes: Props baked into the body are what drift: generate parts as layers.
A seeded model (FLUX Kontext, Seedream) for reproducibility.

snap.description: Image-model output -> pixel art: key the background, detect the model's grid, one colour per cell, remap.
prompt_rules: Snap the WHOLE sheet at once so every frame shares one grid and palette.
Confirm the detected step equals the graph-paper step; reject frames whose step differs; then our remap.
No snapper fixes semantic errors.
notes: Pixel Snapper: 'works best when the source is already close to pixel art'; auto-detect misreads 1:1 art as a 5px grid (always --keep-size for native art).
